feed.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
feed.subtitle: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

entry.title: Trump already tried to hurt Iran with sanctions once - and it didn't work
entry.summary: President Trump is again hoping to use economic pressure to force Iran to the negotiating table.

entry.title: ICE officer faces federal charges in non-fatal shooting in Minneapolis
entry.summary: An ICE officer faces rare federal charges in connection with the non-fatal shooting of a Venezuelan man in Minneapolis.

entry.title: What does it take to run a pizzeria?
entry.summary: For StoryCorps, three siblings discuss what it took for their family to open a beloved neighborhood pizza joint in Brooklyn, N.Y.

entry.title: Work set to begin in Trump's plan for triumphal arch
entry.summary: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks with New York Times reporter Emily Badger about the Trump administration's plans to move forward with construction of a triumphal arch.

entry.title: Forecasters sound the alarm over a powerful El Nino climate pattern
entry.summary: Forecasters expect the El Niño weather pattern to strengthen significantly this year, raising the risks of extreme weather around the world well into 2027.

entry.title: Wesleyan University president on administration's efforts to revoke tax-exempt status
entry.summary: NPR's Steve Inskeep asks Wesleyan University president Michael Roth about U.S. Treasury and IRS efforts to revoke tax-exempt status from private schools that help students based on race.

entry.title: IRS targets private schools that help racial minority students
entry.summary: The Trump administration has said it will end the tax-exempt status for universities with programs that help racial minority students.

entry.title: Scientists study how the brain of a fish filters out signals
entry.summary: The elephantnose fish is native to Africa and a darling of neuroscientists, for its specialized cerebellum-like brain. Scientists have mapped the neurons in a part of the brain that senses electrical signals in detail, and found that how it filters out electrical noise is more complex than they thought.

entry.title: Gloria Steinem, journalist and women's rights activist, remembered
entry.summary: NPR's Michel Martin speaks with Letty Cottin Pogrebin, who cofounded Ms. Magazine with Gloria Steinem about Steinem's legacy.

entry.title: 'How do you know if it's real?' Luxury reseller faces Chanel lawsuit
entry.summary: How do you know if a secondhand luxury good bought online is real? That's at the heart of a lawsuit filed by Chanel against the luxury reseller, The RealReal.
